quests.hint: 'Proposal' is stressed on the second syllable.
quests.explanation: 'Would you mind + -ing' is a polite way to ask for a favor at work.
quests.textToSpeak: Would you mind taking a look at my proposal before I send it to the client?
quests.correctAnswer: Would you mind taking a look at my proposal before I send it to the client?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Proposal' /prəˈpəʊzl/ has a /z/ sound. 'Taking a' links: tay-king-ə. 'Client' /ˈklaɪənt/.

quests.hint: 'Set up' and 'agree on' each work as a unit.
quests.explanation: 'Set up a call' means arrange one, and 'agree on' means reach a shared decision.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll set up a call with the design team so we can agree on a timeline.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll set up a call with the design team so we can agree on a timeline.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Design' /dɪˈzaɪn/ is stressed on ZINE. 'Timeline' /ˈtaɪmlaɪn/ is stressed on TIME. 'Agree on' links.

quests.explanation: English keeps the preposition at the end in this kind of clause: 'what they're responsible for'.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's split the tasks up so that everybody knows exactly what they're responsible for.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's split the tasks up so that everybody knows exactly what they're responsible for.

quests.explanation: Interview answers often pair a personal quality with a working style, joined by 'as well as'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm a quick learner, and I enjoy working in a team as well as independently.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm a quick learner, and I enjoy working in a team as well as independently.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Independently' /ˌɪndɪˈpendəntli/ has five syllables. 'Learner' /ˈlɜːnə/. 'As well as' links: əz-well-əz.

quests.explanation: 'In charge of + -ing' is a common way to describe your responsibilities.
quests.textToSpeak: In my last job, I was in charge of training new staff and organizing weekly meetings.
quests.correctAnswer: In my last job, I was in charge of training new staff and organizing weekly meetings.

quests.explanation: 'What attracted me to… is…' is a strong interview frame that puts your motivation first.
quests.textToSpeak: What attracted me to this position is the chance to develop my skills.
quests.correctAnswer: What attracted me to this position is the chance to develop my skills.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Attracted' /əˈtræktɪd/. 'Develop' /dɪˈveləp/ is stressed on VEL. 'Position' /pəˈzɪʃn/ has /ʃ/. 'Skills' /skɪlz/ starts with /sk/ and ends in /lz/.

quests.explanation: Airline staff use 'I'm afraid' to deliver bad news gently, then offer a solution.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm afraid we've overbooked the flight, so we're offering vouchers to passengers willing to travel tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid we've overbooked the flight, so we're offering vouchers to passengers willing to travel tomorrow.

quests.explanation: 'Must have + past participle' expresses a strong guess about the past, based on evidence.
quests.textToSpeak: My bag must have gone on the wrong plane, because it's not on the belt.
quests.correctAnswer: My bag must have gone on the wrong plane, because it's not on the belt.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Must have' /ˈmʌstəv/. 'Gone' /ɡɒn/. 'Belt' /belt/ ends in /lt/. 'Wrong plane' has /rɒŋ pleɪn/, with a silent 'w' in 'wrong'.

quests.explanation: 'Just as' means at exactly the same moment, and 'which was…' comments on the whole event.
quests.textToSpeak: We got to the platform just as the train was pulling out, which was really frustrating.
quests.correctAnswer: We got to the platform just as the train was pulling out, which was really frustrating.

quests.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession inside a relative clause: 'whose laptop' means 'the colleague's laptop'.
quests.textToSpeak: The colleague whose laptop stopped working yesterday has borrowed one from the IT department.
quests.correctAnswer: The colleague whose laptop stopped working yesterday has borrowed one from the IT department.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Whose' /huːz/. 'Borrowed' /ˈbɒrəʊd/ ends in /d/. 'Department' /dɪˈpɑːtmənt/ is stressed on PART.

quests.hint: 'The shop we went to' has no 'that' or 'which'.
quests.explanation: English often drops the relative pronoun: 'the shop we went to', with 'to' at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: The shop we went to last weekend has closed down, which is a real shame.
quests.correctAnswer: The shop we went to last weekend has closed down, which is a real shame.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Closed' /kləʊzd/ ends in /zd/. 'Shame' /ʃeɪm/. 'Weekend' /ˌwiːkˈend/ often has stress on END here.

quests.explanation: 'Anyone who…' addresses a group, and 'their' is the natural singular pronoun here.
quests.textToSpeak: Anyone who hasn't submitted their form by Friday will need to speak to me directly.
quests.correctAnswer: Anyone who hasn't submitted their form by Friday will need to speak to me directly.

quests.explanation: 'Do you happen to know if…?' is polite, and the clause after 'if' uses statement order.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you happen to know if the bank on the corner is open on Sundays?
quests.correctAnswer: Do you happen to know if the bank on the corner is open on Sundays?

quests.explanation: 'Is likely to' expresses probability, and 'roughly' asks for an estimate.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you tell me how long the appointment is likely to take, roughly?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you tell me how long the appointment is likely to take, roughly?

quests.hint: 'I was just wondering' is one soft chunk.
quests.explanation: Adding 'I was just wondering' makes information questions polite, and the clauses keep statement order.
quests.textToSpeak: I was just wondering what time the last bus leaves, and where it stops.
quests.correctAnswer: I was just wondering what time the last bus leaves, and where it stops.

quests.hint: Use 'were' after 'I' in this advice pattern.
quests.explanation: 'If I were you/in your position' is a standard way to give advice.
quests.textToSpeak: If I were in your position, I'd talk to your manager before making any decisions.
quests.correctAnswer: If I were in your position, I'd talk to your manager before making any decisions.

quests.hint: 'You'd be surprised' is a friendly chunk.
quests.explanation: This sentence uses a mild exaggeration to encourage a habit, and 'in advance' means beforehand.
quests.textToSpeak: You'd be surprised how much time you can save if you plan your week in advance.
quests.correctAnswer: You'd be surprised how much time you can save if you plan your week in advance.

quests.hint: 'Hadn't been for' is quick and weak.
quests.explanation: 'If it hadn't been for' means 'without' in the past, and 'would never have' shows the result that didn't happen.
quests.textToSpeak: If it hadn't been for your help, I would never have finished on time.
quests.correctAnswer: If it hadn't been for your help, I would never have finished on time.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Hadn't' /ˈhædnt/. 'Would never have' /wʊd ˈnevə əv/. 'Finished' /ˈfɪnɪʃt/. 'Time' ends with closed lips.

quests.explanation: Contrastive stress corrects a misunderstanding, and the two verbs are near-synonyms learners often confuse.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't say we should cancel the event, I said we should postpone it.
quests.correctAnswer: I didn't say we should cancel the event, I said we should postpone it.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Postpone' /pəˈspəʊn/ is stressed on SPONE. 'Cancel' /ˈkænsl/. 'Should' is weak /ʃəd/. 'Event' /ɪˈvent/.

quests.explanation: 'It wasn't X who…, it was Y' is a cleft sentence that corrects who did something.
quests.textToSpeak: It wasn't Anna who forgot the tickets, it was Daniel, and he's already apologized.
quests.correctAnswer: It wasn't Anna who forgot the tickets, it was Daniel, and he's already apologized.

quests.explanation: 'The problem isn't X, it's Y' redirects attention to the real issue.
quests.textToSpeak: The problem isn't the price, it's the fact that nobody explained how it works.
quests.correctAnswer: The problem isn't the price, it's the fact that nobody explained how it works.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Explained' /ɪkˈspleɪnd/ ends in /nd/. 'Problem' /ˈprɒbləm/. 'Works' /wɜːks/. 'The fact that' links: thə-fak-that.

quests.explanation: This complaint gives evidence: how many times you've tried and what has happened.
quests.textToSpeak: I've already contacted your support team twice this week, and nobody has replied to my messages.
quests.correctAnswer: I've already contacted your support team twice this week, and nobody has replied to my messages.

quests.explanation: 'Would it be possible to…?' asks politely, and 'someone who can actually resolve' names what you really need.
quests.textToSpeak: Would it be possible to speak to someone who can actually resolve this issue?
quests.correctAnswer: Would it be possible to speak to someone who can actually resolve this issue?

quests.explanation: 'As if it had been opened' uses past perfect to suggest something happened before delivery.
quests.textToSpeak: The product arrived damaged, and the packaging looked as if it had been opened already.
quests.correctAnswer: The product arrived damaged, and the packaging looked as if it had been opened already.

quests.explanation: 'Have been thinking about' shows a decision that has developed over time.
quests.textToSpeak: We've been thinking about relocating for a while, mainly because of the cost of living here.
quests.correctAnswer: We've been thinking about relocating for a while, mainly because of the cost of living here.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Relocating' /ˌriːləʊˈkeɪtɪŋ/. 'Mainly' /ˈmeɪnli/. 'Cost of living' has a steady rhythm: COST-əv-LIV-ing.

quests.explanation: 'Rather than + -ing' contrasts two options, and 'which' comments on the whole choice.
quests.textToSpeak: Rather than driving every day, I've started cycling to work, which has been surprisingly enjoyable.
quests.correctAnswer: Rather than driving every day, I've started cycling to work, which has been surprisingly enjoyable.

quests.hint: Stress 'Thursday' and 'Friday' to mark the timeline.
quests.explanation: 'The plan is to + verb' presents a schedule clearly, which is useful in team meetings.
quests.textToSpeak: The plan is to finish the main work by Thursday and fix small issues on Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: The plan is to finish the main work by Thursday and fix small issues on Friday.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Thursday' /ˈθɜːzdeɪ/. 'Issues' /ˈɪʃuːz/. 'Finish' /ˈfɪnɪʃ/. 'Fix small' joins /fɪks smɔːl/, so slow slightly at the junction.

quests.explanation: 'Although I understand…' acknowledges feelings before disagreeing, and 'on purpose' means deliberately.
quests.textToSpeak: Although I understand why you're upset, I don't think it was done on purpose.
quests.correctAnswer: Although I understand why you're upset, I don't think it was done on purpose.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Upset' /ʌpˈset/ is stressed on SET. 'Purpose' /ˈpɜːpəs/. 'Understand' /ˌʌndəˈstænd/. 'Done on' links: dun-on.

quests.hint: Pause before and after the 'which' clause.
quests.explanation: The 'which' clause adds extra information between commas, and the passive 'has been moved' hides who moved it.
quests.textToSpeak: The workshop, which was originally scheduled for Monday, has been moved to the following week.
quests.correctAnswer: The workshop, which was originally scheduled for Monday, has been moved to the following week.

quests.explanation: 'Keep + -ing' shows a repeated habit, and 'something comes up' is a common excuse.
quests.textToSpeak: I keep telling myself I'll start exercising next week, but then something always comes up.
quests.correctAnswer: I keep telling myself I'll start exercising next week, but then something always comes up.
